selection.name: sqz (C10)
selection.role: Provisional choice for recoverable shell and MCP context compression; report its artifact estimates separately from provider usage.

basis.shows: Claude Code hooks and a cross-client MCP proxy, including Codex; sqz_expand retrieves original content byte for byte. Documents Linux and macOS installation.

Published fixture results retain 76/76 selected facts and verify original recovery. The reported 55.5% reduction uses bytes/4 estimates, includes reporting overhead, and explicitly does not measure live agent task success or provider usage.
Versioned regression tests exercise the real binary, fact preservation, sensitive-content passthrough and byte-exact expansion.
GitHub API reports successful benchmark gates on Linux, macOS and Windows, across stable Rust and Rust 1.85.
Released 2026-09-23; verified CLI and MCP assets for Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64. No GPU is required. Counterfactual transcript replay is explicitly labeled an estimate.
Unarchived repository with a default-branch commit on 2026-09-24, within 90 days.
Issue activity within 90 days: the database-scope question was closed on 2026-08-23.

selection.name: agent-console (C02)
selection.role: Independent Claude Code and Codex usage accounting, with cache classes, missing-data indicators and estimated costs kept separate from compressed artifacts.

basis.shows: Reads local Claude Code and Codex transcripts, including archived Codex sessions. Client integration requires no modification to compression tools.

Defines disjoint input, output, cache-read and cache-write classes; avoids double-counting cached Codex input and reasoning output. Missing classes produce flagged floors, dropped records are counted, and prices remain estimates.
Tests expected accounting totals, copied-transcript and forked-subagent deduplication, delivery-order invariance and disclosure of uncounted records.
GitHub API reports successful tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows with Node 22 and 24; separate parser-fuzz and performance-budget checks also succeeded.
Released 2026-09-27. The documented Node 22+ package archive and standalone Linux x86_64/macOS arm64 assets are actually attached, alongside SHA256SUMS.
Unarchived repository with a default-branch commit on 2026-09-28, within 90 days.
Recent issue activity: a memory-counter integration request opened on 2026-10-01.

excluded.fact: The packet supplies no repository; this is a deployment posture for the separately assessed Context Mode repository.

layers.deciding_comparison: The selected pair leads on documented recovery tests and accounting transparency, not demonstrated end-to-end savings. On the target WSL2 host, compare sqz plus Agent Console against Headroom plus Agent Console and an uncompressed control using matched tasks, client/model versions and repository states. Blind-score task quality; test original recovery after successes, failures and truncation. Include retries, failed attempts, retrieval calls and elapsed time. Record complete provider-reported usage separately from cache subsets, artifact estimates and modeled costs. Separately compare Agent Console and ccusage against identical raw usage records. Repeat representative tasks on macOS arm64.
evidence_gaps: The packet contains no comparison where every named arm ran; reviewed upstream evidence does not establish equal-quality full-provider savings for the recommended combination.
Client transcript accounting can remain incomplete. Agent Console exposes missing classes and dropped records; it does not turn incomplete logs into a complete provider ledger.
Linux and macOS assets and upstream CI were verified, but no clean-host WSL2 installation or live Claude Code/Codex task trial was performed.

The required ctx_fetch_and_index batch was blocked by the session approval policy. Primary documentation, benchmark code and tests were instead retrieved through GitHub API, indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search. Budget used: 30 GitHub API calls, zero web searches, eight requested page fetches with none completed.

Astra/Max review was triggered by conflicting RTK primary documentation. Accepted finding: v0.50.0 documents direct Codex rewriting, while its configuration guide conflicts; working integration on the target client remains unverified.
